TikTok Shop commission rates cluster between 10% and 20% across most categories, but the right number for any product is driven by margin and competition, not the category average. High-margin categories like beauty and supplements can support and often pay toward the top of the range to recruit creators, while thin-margin categories sit lower. Here is how rates vary and how to set yours.

The typical ranges

Treat these as directional, since rates move and vary by product:

  • Beauty and personal care: often 15% to 20%+. High margins and heavy creator competition push rates up.
  • Supplements and wellness: frequently toward the top of the range, for the same reasons.
  • Apparel and accessories: commonly 10% to 20%, depending on margin.
  • Household and home: often 10% to 15%.
  • Tech and electronics: usually lower, 5% to 15%, reflecting thinner margins.
  • Food and beverage: varies widely by margin.

Do not treat a category average as your target. It is a reference point, not a rule.

Before you obsess over the rate, avoid the more common and more expensive mistake. As marketer Neil Patel described it, brands "get serious about TikTok Shop, open the catalog, and pick the highest-margin products" (@neilpatel on X). Margin funds your commission, but if the high-margin product does not sell, no commission rate saves it. Set rates on products that actually move.

Why rates vary

Three forces set the going rate in a category:

  • Margin. High-margin products can afford to pay more. See GMV is not revenue for why margin, not price, is the constraint.
  • Competition for creators. In crowded categories, creators have options, so brands bid up commission to be chosen.
  • Product maturity. New products with no reviews often pay above the norm to overcome the lack of proof.

How to set yours

Do not copy the category; set it from your own numbers:

  1. Calculate true per-unit contribution after all costs.
  2. Decide how much of that room you will share to recruit creators.
  3. Weight your best rate toward hero products you most want promoted.
  4. Go above the category norm when you are new, normalize once you have proof.

Full method in how to set commission rates.

Do not compete on rate alone

A great product at a category-average rate beats a mediocre one at a top rate, because creators earn on volume, not percentage. Fix conversion, reviews, and product first; commission is a lever, not a fix for a weak offer. This is one of the mistakes that kill GMV.

The takeaway

Most categories run 10% to 20%, with high-margin beauty and supplements at the top and thin-margin tech lower, but your rate should come from your margin and competition, not the average. Set it deliberately, weight it toward heroes, and lean higher only when recruiting demands it.
